slides.title: What makes a gadget
slides.text: A gadget has sensors and inputs that collect data, a processor, outputs, maybe storage and a connection, and power.
slides.alt: The step counter brief: small, cheap, lasts all day. A motion sensor and a processor are in; the needs list ticks them off.

focus.cue: The brief: what the gadget must do
The needs: sensor, output, power, processor

slides.title: Sensors
slides.text: A sensor measures the world: light, motion, sound, moisture. A plant waterer needs a moisture sensor to know when the soil is dry.
slides.alt: The plant waterer brief: it needs something that feels dry soil. The moisture sensor is in, and the need is ticked.

focus.cue: A plant waterer needs to feel dry soil
So a moisture sensor goes in

slides.title: Tradeoffs
slides.text: Every part costs money, battery and space. Wireless lets a gadget move freely but uses more battery than a cable. That is a tradeoff.
slides.alt: Too many parts for a step counter: the screen, wireless chip and big battery push the cost, battery and size meters up.
